newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian VSM bond yields 162.86 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russian VSM bond yields 162.86 pct.

text.p: The average yield on a new issue of bonds by RAO Vysokoskorostnye Magistrali (VSM) was 162.86 percent, the central bank said on Thursday.
The 240 billion rouble issue was slightly oversubscribed, but the company, High-Speed Railways in English, raised only 122 billion roubles from the sale.
The central bank has set the first coupon of the bond at 14,151 roubles, or 56.14 percent at an annual rate.
State-owned VSM is building a high-speed rail link between Moscow and St Petersburg.
It issued 120 billion worth of government-backed bonds at the beginning of this year.
The securities are effectively the same as Russian OFZ interest-bearing government bonds. OFZ bonds pay quarterly interest linked to current issues of GKO discount Treasury bills.
VSM's former chairman, Anatoly Zaitsev, was appointed Railways Minister in August. The first head of VSM, Alexei Bolshakov, is now first deputy prime minister.
